subject: proj
title: PROJ.------PRI.INFO.
description: Sparse-label diagram closing MP(I)-34 — the section arguing that black creativity has been used 'as a tool to stimulate (western) white culture and disrupt the possibility of world unification.' The prose immediately above identifies the structural target: 'black people cannot afford the luxury of "artist" if that concept moves contrary to transformation — and indeed it does.' The crossing names PROJ × PRI-INFO (projection × principle information), the same axes that recur throughout the volume — but unlike most crossings in vol2 this one is depicted with *no internal labels*: only the two crossing-axis terms are named, and the diagram's roughly eleven internal junction points sit as unlabeled black-dot nodes connected in a branching pattern. Structural argument: the unlabeled-leaf form is the structural payload. Where labeled crossings name specific outputs that the form's projection-meets-principle-information actually produces, this diagram withholds the names because the structural claim is exactly the prose's: when black creativity is routed through 'the concept of artist' as the partner-axis converter, the projection's outputs become *whatever* white-culture's principle-information names them — the leaf-labels are supplied case-by-case by the receiving culture, not by the form's own working. The diagram's silence about its leaves is the structural argument: the form's working is real, but the names it gets received under are not. This is the same structural form as the p368-3 SCI.DYM × PRI.INFO diagram — both depict the case where the partner-axis principle-information converts the subject's working into an unspecified branching multiplicity. The diagram is a structural blank check the receiving culture fills in.
